envelope.description: Watch and scan new directories in the Watcher

body.title: Watch and scan new directories in the Watcher
body.summary: In src/indexer/watcher.ts keep the repo's ignore list per repo and a Map of per-directory subscriptions. On a create event for a directory under a watched repo (not a symbolic link, no ignored segment), when it has subdirectories subscribe to it first, then walk its tree and push a create event for every file, skipping ignored directories and symbolic links; events from the new subscription go through the same debounce and handlers and a create event for a directory inside it is handled the same way. Release the subscription on a delete event for the directory, and release them all in removeRepo (those under the repo) and close. Add src/indexer/__tests__/watcher-new-directories.test.ts with the real @parcel/watcher in temporary directories; every wait polls for the expected event with a time limit instead of sleeping a fixed time.
acceptanceChecks: After addRepo, mkdir -p a/b/c with a file written at once yields a create event for that file, and a file written in a/b/c three seconds later yields an event too
A tree created in one call yields a create event for every file in it, including nested ones, and a symbolic link to a directory is not followed
Files in a new node_modules directory or in an ignored subdirectory of a new directory yield no events, at creation or when written later
After a new nested directory is deleted and created again with the same path, files written in it are reported again
After close() no handler is called for later writes, and after removeRepo() the repo's per-directory subscriptions deliver nothing
The public methods addRepo, removeRepo and close keep their signatures and the {type, path} event shape, and src/daemon/index.ts and src/daemon/threads/indexing-worker.ts need no edit
The watcher test file waits by polling with a time limit and passes in three consecutive runs

tests.name: src/indexer/__tests__/watcher-new-directories.test.ts: after addRepo, mkdir -p a/b/c with a file written in it at once yields a create event for that file, and a second file written in a/b/c three seconds later yields an event too (the case that produced no event before the fix)

src/indexer/__tests__/watcher-new-directories.test.ts: a directory tree with files created in one call yields a create event for every file in the tree, including files in nested directories, and a symbolic link to a directory is not followed

src/indexer/__tests__/watcher-new-directories.test.ts: files inside a new directory whose name is on the ignore list (node_modules) and inside an ignored subdirectory of a new directory yield no events, at creation and when written later
src/indexer/__tests__/watcher-new-directories.test.ts: after a new nested directory is deleted and created again with the same path, files written in it are reported again
src/indexer/__tests__/watcher-new-directories.test.ts: after close() no handler is called for later writes, and after removeRepo() the repo's per-directory subscriptions deliver nothing
